subject: Action items: hosted quickstart — endpoint mapping and rate-cap experiments
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood-inference.com>
To: Alex Zhou <alex.zhou@parceliq.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Action items: hosted quickstart — endpoint mapping and rate-cap experiments

Thanks again for carving out time today, Alex — great demo and the ParcelIQ product walkthrough was really helpful. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum for the Hosted evaluation: 

Key outcomes from the call:
- ParcelIQ prefers Hosted API for the pilot (keep latency low, avoid infra lift for MVP).
- Expected steady-state workload: ~35 TPS for inference with 4k token average per request; peak bursts up to ~120 TPS for short windows.
- Important: endpoint-level routing (separate routes for shopping-assist vs. post-purchase email generation) and KV/prefix caching for common prompts.

Immediate asks from our side (we can provide these in the sandbox package):
1) Traffic profile spreadsheet (CSV) showing hourly distribution and expected burst windows — helps us size rate caps/auto-burst.
2) Confirmation on success criteria for pilot (latency P99 target, token cost target, and a small quality test set).
3) A preferred date/time for sandbox access (we can provision a staging endpoint and a short-lived key).

What I will do by EOD Monday:
- Share a proposed endpoint matrix (how we recommend mapping your flows to Redwood endpoints) and a quickstart playbook with suggested rate caps and cache hints. (attached: endpoint-matrix-proposal.xlsx, redwood-quickstart-sandbox-playbook.md)
- Provision a sandbox plan and list the minimal telemetry we'll need for a 2-week pilot.

Can you please: 
- Attach the traffic profile CSV (or paste a short sample) — that will unblock rate-cap tuning.
- Confirm whether ParcelIQ needs VPC egress restrictions (IP allowlist) for sandbox or if a standard hosted key is OK for the pilot.

Thanks — short and actionable. If you'd like a 20-minute ops-only call to align on endpoint mapping, happy to schedule tomorrow.

—
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood-inference.com | +1 (415) 555-0129

Attachments: endpoint-matrix-proposal.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood-quickstart-sandbox-playbook.md (markdown)

From: Alex Zhou <alex.zhou@parceliq.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Emily Park <emily.park@parceliq.com>, Platform Ops <ops@parceliq.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Action items: hosted quickstart — endpoint mapping and rate-cap experiments

Ben — thanks for the clear summary. Quick answers inline: 

- We are aligned on Hosted for the pilot. Long-term we may evaluate Dedicated if cost per token and throughput economics point that way, but pilot should be Hosted.
- I'll attach a sample hour-by-hour traffic export from our event system (see parceliq-traffic-profile.csv attached). Expect a daily peak between 11:00-12:30 PT and a secondary evening peak 18:30-19:15 PT.
- P99 latency target for user-facing flows: <= 350ms for up to 4k tokens. Cost target: keep inference cost below $0.03 per user interaction on average during the pilot.
- On network restrictions: ops team prefers IP allowlist for sandbox keys. Ops, I copied you to confirm exact CIDR ranges.

Two quick questions for Redwood: 
1) How do you recommend we carve endpoints? We have three logical flows: 
   a) Shopping-assist (low-latency, high qps)
   b) Abandoned-cart email generation (batch, larger context)
   c) Post-purchase personalization (medium qps, uses KV cache)
2) For burst periods, do you support short-term transient bursting above committed rates, and if so what does auto-fallback look like (model variant fallback vs queued requests)?

Should be able to review your endpoint matrix this afternoon. Thanks — Alex

—
Alex Zhou
Head of Product, ParcelIQ
alex.zhou@parceliq.com

Attachment: parceliq-traffic-profile.csv

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood-inference.com>
To: Alex Zhou <alex.zhou@parceliq.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Action items: hosted quickstart — endpoint mapping and rate-cap experiments

Alex — perfect, thanks for the traffic sample and the clarity on objectives. A few concrete proposals based on the profile you shared: 

Endpoint mapping (proposed):
- /v1/endpoint/shopping-assist — lightweight model variant, tuned for low-latency; conservative per-route rate cap with aggressive auto-burst for short windows; P99 SLA target 300–350ms.
- /v1/endpoint/abandoned-cart — batch-friendly endpoint, allow larger context sizes and higher token ceilings; best-effort latency SLA (we can accept higher P99 here).
- /v1/endpoint/post-purchase — medium-latency endpoint with prefix/KV caching enabled (we'll recommend a 2nd-level cache TTL for common profile prompts).

Burst behavior and fallbacks:
- Hosted supports transient auto-burst above configured route caps for short windows (configurable burst window and total tokens). If burst exceeds safe limits we can automatically fallback to a smaller model variant for the shopping-assist endpoint (preserves availability). We will include a canary policy and a fallback rollout you can opt into for the pilot.

Next steps (action items):
- Redwood: provision sandbox endpoints and temporary API key with IP allowlist — ETA 24 hours once you confirm CIDRs. (attached: redwood-quickstart-sandbox-playbook.md)
- ParcelIQ: confirm CIDR ranges for ops and share any internal test keys we should accept. (Emily / Ops)
- Shared: agree on a 7–14 day pilot window and 3 pilot success metrics (latency P99, average cost per interaction, and quality pass-rate on the test prompts).

I put a short checklist in the shared Drive link (see related_links) — I'll also drop a compact test prompt set and a lightweight telemetry schema you can send back for quality checks.

If it helps, Marissa can run a 20-minute ops onboarding tomorrow morning to step through sandbox keys and the telemetry payload. Marissa — are you available 9:30–10:00am PT?

—
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood-inference.com | +1 (415) 555-0129

Attachments: redwood-quickstart-sandbox-playbook.md

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood-inference.com>
To: Alex Zhou <alex.zhou@parceliq.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Sat, 31 Mar 2028 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Action items: hosted quickstart — endpoint mapping and rate-cap experiments

Thanks team — quick confirm from ops side: we can provision sandbox API key with an IP allowlist and a 48-hour rolling key rotation if ParcelIQ wants. Alex — can you provide the CIDRs and the list of test client IPs? Once we have those we will set up the key and post the credentials to the secure stub in the drive link.

Also flagging one compliance ask: for the pilot please let us know if you need SOC 2 evidence or specific logging retention longer than 30 days — that will change the telemetry plan but not the quickstart timeline.

If no objections I'll schedule a 30-minute onboarding for Monday 9:30am PT to walk through endpoints and the telemetry schema.

—
Neha Kapoor
Customer Success Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood-inference.com
